projects.title: 我们准备在大学一年级 C 语言课程中允许学生使用生成式 AI 编程助手。它到底会不会提高学习效果？应该怎样引入？
projects.title_en: 大一 C 语言课程是否应该允许学生使用生成式 AI 编程助手？
projects.question: 我们准备在大学一年级 C 语言课程中允许学生使用生成式 AI 编程助手。它到底会不会提高学习效果？应该怎样引入？

decision.decision_question: 大一 C 语言课程是否应该允许学生使用生成式 AI 编程助手？
decision.target_population: university first-year computer science students learning C programming for the first time
decision.target_context: 16-week lecture-lab course, 60 students, TA support, offline
supported_claims: AI coding assistants reliably increase task performance during training (completion speed, correctness) — E-001, E-006.
Unguarded generative AI access can harm independent problem solving when access is removed — E-004.
Guardrail design (hints instead of answers) substantially mitigates the negative learning effect — E-005.
Task performance gains do not automatically imply learning gains — E-004 vs E-006 (within-study contrast).
Tool capability is substantial: Codex solves roughly half to three-quarters of CS1 exam-style questions — E-010.
Professional-developer RCT shows ~55% faster task completion with Copilot; directness limited by professional population — E-008.
LLM code explanations rate comparable to student-authored explanations, viable as scaffold material — E-011.
uncertain_claims: Whether AI coding assistants improve or preserve actual programming learning in university novices — no direct university-level RCT in reviewed set [无直接证据]
Whether one-week neutral retention (Kazemitabaar 2023) extends to a semester — E-003.
Whether benchmark quality findings (E-009) and explanation-quality ratings (E-011) translate into classroom learning gains.
How comprehension/ownership difficulties documented in usability studies (E-012) behave over a full semester with guardrails.
contradicted_claims: The claim 'AI tools always improve learning' is contradicted by E-004 (unguarded access, -17% independent exam).
The claim 'speed gains equal learning gains' is contradicted by the task-vs-learning separation across E-001/E-006/E-008 vs E-004.
decision.reason_for_disagreement: Disagreement comes from outcome separation (task vs learning), tool design (guarded vs unguarded), and population (K-12 / professionals vs university). Task-performance evidence is consistently positive across randomized and benchmark studies; the only study measuring independent performance after AI removal shows harm without guardrails; usability and artifact studies add dependence and quality caveats rather than resolving the learning question.
decision.methodology_summary: Eight real sources: three randomized experiments (Kazemitabaar 2023 n=69 K-12; Bastani 2025 n≈950 high-school mathematics; Peng 2023 n=95 professional developers, preprint), one ESL writing mixed-methods study (Marzuki 2024), plus benchmark/capability/usability studies (Yetistiren 2023; Finnie-Ansley 2022; explanation-comparison 2023; Vaithilingam 2022). No direct RCT in university programming courses. Internal validity of the core RCTs is strong; directness to first-year university C programming is weak. All sources carry registry-verified DOIs (see benchmarks/doi-audit/report.md).

outcome_specific_findings.completion_time: positive during training and professional tasks (E-001, E-008)
outcome_specific_findings.assignment_score: positive during practice, negative on closed-book exam (E-004, E-006); tool itself scores passing-level on CS1 questions (E-010)
outcome_specific_findings.code_quality: mixed on benchmarks; security concerns documented (E-009)
outcome_specific_findings.metacognition: LLM explanations compare well (E-011) while novice ownership/debugging difficulties persist (E-012)
outcome_specific_findings.ai_dependency: documented crutch behavior with unguarded tool (E-004, E-005, E-012)

decision.short_term_effect: Task performance reliably increases; learning effect null-to-negative without guardrails.
decision.long_term_effect: No evidence beyond one week; long-term learning effect unknown.
decision.transfer_effect: No full transfer evidence; manual code-modification not harmed in one small study (E-002).
decision.risk_effect: AI dependency and over-reliance risk is real and documented for unguarded usage (E-004) and foreshadowed by usability findings (E-012).

applicability.suitable_for: pilot in first-year C course with guardrailed usage policy
applicability.not_suitable_for: unrestricted AI adoption without usage policy
required_conditions: guardrailed AI usage policy (hints not answers, modeled on GPT Tutor arm)

what_can_be_claimed: AI coding assistants raise task performance for novices during training.
Unguarded access carries a real risk of hurting independent problem solving.
Guardrail design can mitigate that risk.
Direct evidence for university C programming learning is missing.
Tool capability headroom is large (CS1 question pass rates; professional speed RCT).
what_cannot_be_claimed: AI coding assistants improve (or even preserve) university students' programming learning.
Any claim about which students benefit, based on university samples.
That benchmark or usability findings substitute for classroom learning outcomes.
missing_evidence: RCT of AI coding assistants in university programming courses with retention and no-AI transfer tests.
Studies varying AI usage policy within the same course.
Longitudinal data on AI dependency beyond one course.
Peer-reviewed replication of the professional speed RCT (Peng et al. remains a preprint).
decision.decision_rationale: Positive task-performance evidence plus documented unguarded-access risk, mixed quality/usability signals, and missing university-level learning evidence → bounded, guardrailed pilot with evaluation, not full adoption.
exceeds_evidence_boundary: Claiming 'AI coding assistants improve learning' exceeds the boundary: direct learning-effect evidence is missing.
Claiming 'AI works for everyone' exceeds the boundary: population and subject mismatch.

Unguarded generative AI access can harm independent problem solving when access is removed — E-004.

Task performance gains do not automatically imply learning gains — E-004 vs E-006 (within-study contrast).
Tool capability is substantial: Codex solves roughly half to three-quarters of CS1 exam-style questions — E-010.
Professional-developer RCT shows ~55% faster task completion with Copilot; directness limited by professional population — E-008.
LLM code explanations rate comparable to student-authored explanations, viable as scaffold material — E-011.

projects.title: 企业客服团队是否应引入生成式 AI 助手？
projects.title_en: Should an enterprise customer-support team introduce a generative AI assistant?
projects.question: Should an enterprise customer-support team introduce a generative AI assistant?

decision.decision_question: Should an enterprise customer-support team introduce a generative AI assistant?
decision.target_population: Enterprise customer-support staff, stratified by tenure and baseline skill.
decision.target_context: Human-supervised support using an approved knowledge base.
supported_claims: AI assistance can shorten customer chat handling in a bounded support setting; throughput is a separate outcome.
ChatGPT reduced time on short professional writing tasks; this is indirect evidence for customer support.
AI can reduce correctness on tasks outside its capability frontier; consulting evidence is indirect for support.
Experienced, high-skill support staff need separate quality monitoring rather than assumed uniform benefits.
uncertain_claims: Local net cost, privacy incident rates, subgroup service quality and sustained performance are not established by this selected evidence set.
decision.decision_rationale: A supervised pilot is warranted because one direct field study supports efficiency gains but also reveals heterogeneous quality effects. Indirect experiments identify task boundaries, while local safety and net value remain unknown.
decision.methodology_summary: One staggered-rollout quasi-experiment and two randomized experiments. Only the support study is direct; no pooled standardized effect or model benchmark was computed.
what_cannot_be_claimed: Universal gains, autonomous deployment safety, privacy protection, reduced staffing requirements or educational learning gains.
missing_evidence: Local net cost, privacy incident rates, subgroup service quality and sustained performance are not established by this selected evidence set.

required_conditions: Start with low-risk, knowledge-base-covered queues; agents inspect and edit every proposed reply.
Stratify by tenure and baseline skill; retain expert discretion and measure review workload.
Minimize and redact customer data, restrict access and retention, and review supplier data-use terms before a pilot.
Escalate unfamiliar, ambiguous, sensitive or high-stakes requests to qualified humans; no autonomous commitments.

extensions.note: Conservative manual judgment about broad deployment; not a deterministic confidence-policy run or a probability.

knowledge_gaps.summary: Local net cost, privacy incident rates, subgroup service quality and sustained performance are not established by this selected evidence set.
